_about: Engine-local search material only: per theme one X advanced-search term, one LinkedIn search-bar string and one keyword set, which no other runtime needs. The two search strings are not interchangeable - X operators (OR, lang:en, -filter:replies, negated words) mean nothing to LinkedIn search, so each theme carries its own. LinkedIn is only read when listen.py is called with --linkedin; a default pass makes no LinkedIn call and spends nothing there. Everything else a theme carries - what it is, why it is different, the fact it links back to, cleared partner tags, intro-post state, layer, licence, logics and licence basis - is read from .atelier/memory/themes.md, and every handle and cleared name from .atelier/memory/handles.md. scripts/memory.py is this engine's read path into them; the roster of themes comes from themes.md and is joined to the terms below by tag, so a term with no theme row (or a theme row with no term) is an error, not a silent skip. Empty until themes.md has rows: add one entry per hashtag, keyed by the hashtag, with x_search, linkedin_search and keywords.

_source_of_truth._note: The stealth denylist lives in .atelier/memory/handles.private.md. That file is gitignored and is merged on top of .atelier/memory/handles.md at read time; it carries the denylist terms plus the stealth and unsigned-draft parties. No copy lives in this repository's committed files. gate_lint blocks, never passes, when the companion is expected and absent.

#ExampleTheme.x_search: an X advanced-search term of at most 255 characters, registered verbatim as a twitterapi.io filter rule by scripts/x_stream.py
#ExampleTheme.linkedin_search: a LinkedIn search-bar string, no operators
keywords: that mark a result as on-theme

mentions._about: Brand and adjacency mentions. Not a theme; feeds interaction proposals and the engager ledger. Empty x_search means no mentions pass is run.

ignore._about: Another stream's chatter. Listening drops any result whose text names one of these, in listen.py and in the stream (x_stream.py); the mentions term also excludes them at the source. The theme terms carry no exclusion, since the stream registers each verbatim and several may sit near the 255-character cap.
